# Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 11 (Bi-Vb Pc11)
**ID:** Bi-Vb Pc11
**Section:** Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga (bi-vb)
**Collection:** Vinaya

**Title (English, from literature):** Meeting a man in the dark

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 11, entitled *Rattandhakāra* ("Meeting a man in the dark"), governs situations where a Buddhist nun remains alone in darkness with a male interlocutor [SuttaCentral; Hüsken 1997]. The rule establishes that if a nun, one-on-one, stands together with or converses with a man in the darkness of night where there is no light (*yā pana bhikkhunī rattandhakāre appadīpe purisena saddhiṁ eken’ ekā santiṭṭheyya vā sallapeyya vā*), she incurs an offense requiring confession (*pācittiya*) [SuttaCentral; Hüsken 1997]. In the background origin story, a nun is depicted standing and speaking with a male relative [Hüsken 1997]. Commenting on this formulation, the *Samantapāsādikā* glosses "without light" (*appadīpe*) as a place unilluminated by any lamp, moon, sun, or fire [Hüsken 1997].
While there is no identical rule in the Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga, Pācittiya 11 forms the beginning of a cohesive sequence of four Bhikkhunī rules (Pācittiyas 11–14) that forbid nuns from standing together with or conversing with a man in specific secluded or compromising circumstances, such as in the dark, in hidden places, or on public streets and crossroads [Hüsken 1997]. An English translation of the text is provided by Bhikkhu Brahmali [SuttaCentral].
Curated parallels to the rule exist across the Vinaya traditions of multiple early schools, including the Pali Bhikkhunī Pātimokkha and Parivāra, the Chinese recensions of the Dharmaguptaka (*Pc 86*), Mahīśāsaka (*Pc 128*), Sarvāstivāda (*Pc 84*), and Mahāsāṅghika (*Pc 123*), as well as the Sanskrit Mahāsāṅghika-Lokottaravādin Bhikṣuṇī Vibhaṅga (*san-lo-bi-vb-pc123*) [SuttaCentral]. DharmaNexus highlights extensive Pali-internal text reuse with structurally similar Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga rules, most notably Pācittiyas 12, 13, and 14, as well as cross-language alignments with the Tibetan Vinayavibhaṅga (D0003-3) and later commentary literature [DharmaNexus].
